title: Intake clarity: runtime footprint metadata and pinning-exceptions for fast-track open-models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Recent intake of experimental open models exposed ambiguity in the catalog metadata schema: teams are unsure which runtime-level signals are required to make a pinning decision and when a temporary pin-exception can be granted for fast-track ingest. Scope: define a compact, actionable set of runtime footprint fields and a short-lived pin-exception flow for curated fast-track open-models (beta/adoptable). Goals: 1) reduce review friction for Model Catalog reviewers and runtime oncall; 2) ensure safe runtime compatibility and clear rollback criteria when an unpinned ingest is admitted; 3) provide measurable acceptance criteria for automated sanity checks in the intake pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog intake form includes required runtime footprint fields: peak_memory_gb, typical_max_seq, avg_tokens_per_call, kv_cache_compat (yes/no), quantization_support (list of tags), and kernel_notes (free text).
Metadata mapping documented with exact expected units and example values; runtime-1.19 automated validator can parse and reject malformed footprint entries.

Pin-exception workflow defined: criteria for 'fast-track' (e.g., community weight provenance, eval parity score >= 0.92, non-adversarial license), timebox (30 days), and mandatory canary deployment steps.
SRE/perf signoff checklist created: mandatory smoke-tests (latency p50/p95 delta < +25% vs baseline, throughput regression < 15%), and a KV-cache memory leak check during 48h canary.
Fallback policy specified: automatic fallback to pinned compatible variant or model-lite variant if p95 latency exceeds SLO for 15 minutes or error_rate > 3% for 5 minutes.
Every granted pin-exception emits an audit entry with owner, rationale, and expiration date; Console surfaces these exceptions on the model details page.
Automated alerts and a short Playbook entry added to runbook for handling fast-track regressions and rollback.
notes: Design trade-off: collecting more runtime signals reduces runtime surprises but increases intake friction; we selected a minimal set that maps to runtime scheduling heuristics.
We opted for a 30-day max pin-exception to limit blast radius while giving partners time to publish a pinned variant.
PM asked to include a simple binary 'kv_cache_compat' flag to triage models that rely heavily on prefix caching vs those that do not.
Engineering requested kernel_notes to capture non-standard ops or fused kernels that might affect runtime portability.
SRE requested the canary policy include a memory growth/GC metric sample every 10 minutes; added to acceptance criteria as part of smoke-tests.
